basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: Describes the end-to-end stages by which a beneficiary receives value, not the steps or tasks that perform the work.
Starts from a trigger and ends in a terminal outcome class that matters to the beneficiary.
Stage order and value states are versioned definitions, separate from any observed realization.
Differs from a process or workflow, which defines how activities are executed and by whom.

may: Draft a value stream definition with trigger, stages, entry and exit criteria and terminal outcome.
Link a value stream version to realizations, objectives and observations owned elsewhere.
Compare two definition versions and report changed stages.
Flag stages that have no realizing process or capability.
mustNot: Edit a published definition version in place instead of issuing a new one.
Treat a value stream map as a process specification or as authority to reorganize work.
Assign performance targets to named people from value stream metrics alone.
Merge streams with different beneficiaries into one definition.
requiresHuman: Approving a value stream definition as an official version.
Retiring a value stream that strategy or funding decisions reference.
Choosing the beneficiary and the enterprise boundary.

considerations: Choosing whose value counts decides whose needs drive redesign; secondary beneficiaries can be left out.
Value stream analysis is often used to justify cutting roles, and the people affected should have a voice.
Outcome measures should reflect real benefit to the beneficiary, not only internal efficiency.
affectedParties: Customers and other beneficiaries of the stream
Staff who perform the realizing processes
Decision makers who fund and prioritize stages

items: A value stream has a named beneficiary, a triggering event, an ordered set of value-adding stages and a terminal outcome.
It is confused with a process model, a customer journey map and a lean value stream map of material flow.
Redesign based on an outdated stream definition.
Benefits claimed for a stage that has no realization behind it.
Local optimization of one stage that harms the end-to-end outcome.
The Open Group ArchiMate value stream element.
TOGAF Series Guide on value streams.
BIZBOK Guide value stream mapping practice.
OMG BPMN 2.0 for linking realizing processes.
